title: By the bright morning, after a hard silence.
subtitle: An oath that opens a message of comfort
then: Jibril was slow in coming for a time, and the Prophet ﷺ was affected by it. {trap}The idolaters said: his Lord has abandoned him.{/trap} This surah came in reply. Allah swears by {reward}the forenoon and the light He placed in it{/reward}.
now: You prayed for weeks about something and heard nothing. Someone even said, maybe God is not listening to you. {reward}The surah opens with morning light{/reward}, the thing that always comes back after the dark.
old: When my prayers feel unanswered, it means I have been left.
new: A quiet stretch is not a goodbye; the morning still comes.
try: Tomorrow, step into the morning light for a minute and remember a prayer that was answered.

title: And by the night, when it settles still.
subtitle: Darkness that rests, not darkness that ends
then: Mujahid, Qatadah and others said the night here {idea}settles, darkens and covers{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says light and dark both prove the power of their Creator. He cites: {idea}He appointed the night for resting{/idea}.
now: A slow season at work, or a dry patch in your worship, feels like a punishment. {idea}Nights are not punishments. They are pauses.{/idea} The same Hand that brings the night brings the morning.
old: A dark season means something has gone wrong.
new: The night is made by the same Lord as the morning, and it has its own purpose.
try: Tonight, rest on purpose. Put the phone away early and sleep.

title: Your Lord has not left you, and He is not angry.
subtitle: The direct answer to the fear
then: Jundub reported that when the Prophet ﷺ was ill and did not stand for prayer for a night or two, a woman mocked him. {reward}Allah replied: your Lord has neither forsaken you nor hates you.{/reward} The introduction says the pause gave him rest, {idea}not a sign of displeasure{/idea}.
now: You slipped up, then things got hard, and you decided Allah was angry and gone. {reward}This verse was said to the most beloved person to Allah, at his lowest moment.{/reward} The fear you feel is not proof.
old: If life gets heavy, Allah must be displeased with me.
new: Allah's silence for a while is not His leaving, and hardship is not His hatred.
try: Say this verse's meaning out loud to yourself once today: my Lord has not left me.

title: What comes later is better than what is now.
subtitle: The Hereafter is better than this first life
then: Ibn Mas'ud saw the straw mat leave marks on the Prophet's ﷺ side and offered something soft. He said: {idea}the parable of me and this world is like a rider who rests in the shade of a tree, then passes on{/idea}. {reward}He chose what is with Allah.{/reward}
now: You scroll through house listings and holiday photos, and your own life looks small. {idea}You are a rider under a tree.{/idea} The shade is good. It is not where you are going.
old: This life is the main event.
new: This life is the shade on the road; what is ahead is better.
try: When you feel envy today, say quietly: what is with Allah is better.

title: Your Lord will give you until you are satisfied.
subtitle: A promise of generosity, not a bare minimum
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah will give him {reward}until He pleases him concerning his followers{/reward}, and from what He has prepared for him, including Al-Kawthar. When this was said, he had almost nothing. The introduction calls it {idea}a prophecy that came literally true{/idea}.
now: You are in the hard first years: the small flat, the junior job, the bills. {reward}This verse was said to someone with far less.{/reward} Allah's giving is not measured in what you can see right now.
old: Things will probably always be about this hard.
new: Allah's promise is to give until I am content, even when I cannot see how.
try: Write down one hope you have stopped asking for. Ask for it again tonight.

title: You were an orphan, and He gave you a home.
subtitle: Looking back to see who was caring for you
then: His father died before he was born, his mother {idea}Aminah{/idea} when he was six. His grandfather Abdul-Muttalib took him in, then his uncle {reward}Abu Talib{/reward}, who protected him for decades. Ibn Kathir calls all this Allah's protection and care.
now: You remember the hard year: the move, the loss, the lonely school. Then you remember the teacher who noticed you, the aunt who took you in. {reward}You were never as alone as it felt.{/reward}
old: Nobody was looking out for me back then.
new: Looking back, Allah kept sending someone to shelter me.
try: Think of one person who sheltered you when you were young. Send them a thank-you message.

title: You did not know the way, and He guided you.
subtitle: Guidance that came as a gift
then: Ibn Kathir links this to the verse: {idea}you knew not what is the Book, nor what is faith{/idea}, but We made it a light. Before revelation the Prophet ﷺ did not have this knowledge. {reward}Allah gave it.{/reward}
now: You remember who you were before you started praying, or before you came back to it. You did not reason your way there alone. {reward}Something opened a door.{/reward} That opening was a gift.
old: My faith is something I worked out by myself.
new: Whatever guidance I have was given to me, and I can thank Him for it.
try: Recall the moment faith first meant something to you, and thank Allah for it in sujood.

title: You were in need, and He made you enough.
subtitle: Poverty, then richness of the soul
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}made him independent of all others besides Him{/reward}, so he knew both being poor and patient, and wealthy and thankful. The Prophet ﷺ said: {idea}wealth is the richness of the soul{/idea}.
now: You compare your salary to a friend's and feel poor, though your fridge is full and your rent is paid. {idea}The verse points at a different kind of enough.{/idea} {reward}A soul that is content is rich.{/reward}
old: I will feel secure once I have more.
new: Real wealth is a soul made content by Allah, whatever the account says.
try: List three things you already have that you once prayed for.

title: You were an orphan, so never crush an orphan.
subtitle: Turning what you received into how you treat others
then: Ibn Kathir: {idea}just as you were an orphan and Allah sheltered you, do not oppress the orphan{/idea}. Do not humiliate, scorn or despise him; be kind and gentle. Qatadah said: {reward}be like a merciful father to the orphan{/reward}.
now: There is a kid in your child's class whose dad is gone. At the birthday party he hangs back. {reward}You can be the adult who notices him.{/reward} The kindness you got once is meant to pass through you.
old: Other people's kids are not my responsibility.
new: The care I received is meant to pass through me to someone without it.
try: Do one kind thing this week for a child who has lost a parent, or give to an orphan fund.

title: Do not push away the one who asks.
subtitle: Whether they ask for help or for knowledge
then: Ibn Kathir: just as you were unaware and guided, {idea}do not scorn the one who asks for knowledge{/idea}. Ibn Ishaq said do not be arrogant or mean to the weak. Qatadah said: {reward}respond to the poor with mercy and gentleness{/reward}.
now: A new colleague asks the same basic question twice. A man asks for change outside the station. Your first reflex is a sigh. {reward}You can say no kindly, or yes gently, but not with a shove.{/reward}
old: Some questions and requests are just annoying.
new: The one asking me is a chance to pass on what I was given.
try: Next time someone asks you something today, answer slowly and kindly.

title: Speak about your Lord's blessing on you.
subtitle: Gratitude that is said out loud

key.label: Two ways to hold a blessing

then: Ibn Kathir: just as you were poor and Allah made you rich, {idea}tell about Allah's favor upon you{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}whoever is not thankful to people is not thankful to Allah{/reward}.
now: Someone asks how you are and you say "fine, tired, busy." Your child is healthy, you have work, you got through a hard year. {reward}You could say alhamdulillah and mean it.{/reward} Not a brag. A thank-you.
old: Talking about my blessings sounds like showing off.
new: Mentioning Allah's favor with humility is a way of thanking Him.
try: Tell one person today about something good Allah gave you, and thank someone who helped.
